title: Prompt set
description: The questions this brand's visibility is measured against, and the fourth frozen artifact after business.json, clusters.json and briefs. Keywords are what people TYPE INTO A SEARCH BOX; prompts are what they ASK A MODEL, and the two are different shapes: 'best adhd planner' and 'I have ADHD and keep abandoning planners, what should I use' retrieve differently and name different brands. Generated from approved clusters plus business.json, approved by a human, then FROZEN. Freezing matters more here than anywhere else in the pipeline: if the set drifts, month-to-month numbers are not comparable and you will draw confident conclusions from noise.

brand.description: The name a model would have to say for a mention to count.

aliases.description: Other ways the brand might be written. A mention check that only looks for the exact name undercounts.

set_id.description: Stable id for this frozen set, e.g. 2026-Q4. Every measurement records it, so a comparison across two different sets can be refused rather than silently reported as change.

confirmed_at.description: The gate. Null means the set is not approved and no measurement should run against it.

prompts.description: Fewer than a handful cannot measure anything, given how much answers vary run to run.

text.description: Phrased the way a person would actually ask, not the keyword with a question mark bolted on.

archetype.description: A fixed set on purpose. A prompt set made only of 'best X' questions measures one narrow thing and reports it as visibility.

expect_mention.description: Should this brand plausibly appear? Not every prompt should. Including prompts you SHOULD NOT win is what stops a set being self-flattering, and absence on those is a correct result rather than a failure.

win_condition.description: What counts as success. Being named in passing is not the same as being the recommendation, and measuring them as one number hides which you actually got.

competitors_expected.description: Who you would expect a model to name here. Used for share of voice, and for noticing when a rival you never tracked keeps appearing.
